See the engineer’s judgment in the work
Decide whether candidates can use AI
Allow the AI Assistant or turn it off for each task, and every prompt and response is saved for review. Account administrators can also switch off all AI features. Integrity signals support human review in either case.
Put Claude Code and Codex into the assessment
Candidates use Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex CLI in the VS Code terminal alongside project tools, so they work with the AI tools they already use. The full interaction is saved to the report and covered by Replay. In Interview, both participants can use it live.
Choose tasks that test how engineers use AI
Ask candidates to debug, investigate or build with an assistant. Some tasks include deliberate assistant errors to check and correct. For AI engineering roles, assess candidates building AI or machine learning systems.
Review the solution and how it developed
Replay the code and AI exchanges to see what candidates asked, accepted and fixed. Each AI skill comes with a quote from their prompts.

A conventional coding exercise can show whether the final solution works. An AI detection tool addresses a different question: whether assistance may have been used.
Codility puts the assistant into the task and preserves the interaction. Reviewers examine the candidate’s work and decisions, supported by documented assessment methodology.

Assessing engineers with AI in the workflow
Claude Code and Codex run in the Codility assessment environment across Screen, Interview and Skills Intelligence. Every interaction is saved to the record. Account and assessment settings control access.
An administrator can turn all AI features off across the account. Assessments can also disable the AI Assistant individually. Integrity checks remain available for human review.
Behavioral and similarity checks
can surface signals of undisclosed assistance. Reviewers inspect the evidence behind the risk rating. No signal proves misconduct on its own, and a reviewer makes every decision.
AI usage metrics and the AI skills the report shows do not change automatic task scores. Selected task types use fixed scoring rules. In a live interview, the human interviewer assesses the candidate against the rubric.
